assignments.reason: This node IS the act of mishpat — judging all one's affairs ('יכלכל דבריו במשפט'). Its essential nature is self-judgment, which is the defining quality of Package 3. It appears as a cause in multiple eitza edges (producing fear-removal, yirah-elevation, etc.), but what it IS is the practical execution of mishpat. The node is effectively an elaborated form of the משפט concept.

This node describes the elevation/raising of yirah — its essential nature is yirah in motion (ascending). While mishpat is the MEANS of elevation, the node itself ('elevating the yirah') is about yirah's ascent, which is the core dynamic of Package 1 (the yirah cluster, which already contains 'עלית היראה לשרשה'). The concept is yirah being purified and raised, not the mechanism (mishpat) that raises it.

Removing all fears is the negative formulation of purifying yirah — stripping away the false fears (yirah clothed in klipa) so that only true yirat Hashem remains. Its essential nature is yirah-purification. The fears (pachad) are the impure form of yirah; removing them IS the process of yirah returning to its holy root. This belongs in the yirah cluster (Package 1), not in mishpat (which is the tool that achieves this).

This IS yirah rising from the klipa and the nations — yirah in its transitional state, ascending from impurity to holiness. Its essential nature is yirah itself (the quality of awe/fear) in the act of being redeemed. Package 1 already contains the concept of עלית היראה לשרשה (yirah ascending to its root); this node captures the same dynamic from the perspective of where yirah is coming FROM (the klipa).

assignments.node_id: תשאר אך יראת־השם ולא יראה אחרת
assignments.reason: This IS pure yirat Hashem — the refined, holy form of yirah that remains after all foreign fears are removed. Its essential nature is yirah in its perfected state: 'only fear of God and no other fear.' This is the culmination and purest expression of the yirah cluster (Package 1). It is the RESULT of mishpat, but what it IS is yirah at its holiest.

assignments.node_id: ואין היראה מתלבש בשום דבר לעורר את האדם, כי הוא בעצמו נתעורר
assignments.reason: This describes the state where yirah is no longer clothed in external things to arouse the person, because the person arouses himself through self-judgment. Its essential nature is the liberated state of yirah — yirah freed from its klipa garments. The node describes what happens TO yirah (it stops being clothed in worldly fears), making it fundamentally about the yirah domain. The person's self-arousal is the sign that yirah has been purified.

The ascent of yirah to the level of daat — this IS yirah in its ascending movement toward its root. Package 1 already contains 'עלית היראה לשרשה' (the frog = yirah ascending to its root). This node is nearly identical in essential nature: yirah rising to daat. While daat is the destination (Package 2), the node describes the ASCENT of yirah, and the subject of the sentence is yirah, not daat.

To raise the attribute of yirah to its root — this is the Torah's opening thesis statement (section א). Its essential nature is yirah-elevation, the core aspiration of the entire teaching. It is functionally synonymous with 'עלית היראה לשרשה' already in Package 1. The root (daat) is the destination, but the concept itself is about yirah's movement upward.

assignments.node_id: שמקשרין היראה על־ידי משפט לבחינת דעת
assignments.reason: This compound node describes the complete causal mechanism: connecting yirah via mishpat to daat. Its essential nature is the ACT of connecting — the mechanism. While it references yirah and daat, the active agent and distinctive content is mishpat as the connecting tool. The Torah's summary statement (section ז) frames this as the function of Israel/mishpat: 'ישראל שהם בחינת משפט הם מעלין ומקשרין'. The verb 'מקשרין' (connecting) is the mishpat-action.

Attaining/comprehending Torah — this IS Torah (its essential nature is Torah knowledge). Section ד states: 'when one reaches daat, one merits the attainment of Torah.' The concept being attained is Torah itself. While daat is the prerequisite (cause), the node describes the TORAH that is attained. In context, this refers to Torah in general, which the Rebbe then divides into nigleh and nistar; at the initial stage, it aligns with Torah shebenigleh (the first level of Torah attainment via daat), as the Rebbe says 'the dwelling of Torah is with the person of daat.'

Prayer with self-sacrifice — this IS tefillah in its highest form. Its essential nature is prayer (Package 5), specifically prayer elevated to the level of total self-nullification. The additions file notes it 'functions as a causal precondition' for hidden Torah, but its NATURE is prayer. The Rebbe frames it as the raven-quality of prayer: praying without any self-interest, becoming cruel to oneself like a raven to its young. It is the Abraham/chesed dimension of prayer taken to its extreme.

God becomes 'as if' in the aspect of a woman (receiving) — this describes the divine response to prayer. Its essential nature belongs to the prayer domain: it is the reciprocal aspect of tefillah, where God receives pleasure from Israel's prayer ('ריח ניחוח לה'). The metaphor of 'isha' (woman/receiving) describes what prayer ACCOMPLISHES in the divine realm. While it could be seen as a separate theological concept, in this Torah it functions entirely within the prayer framework — it is the chesed-dimension of prayer (God's chesed in receiving our prayer), which is Package 5's core theme.

assignments.node_id: ואינו חושב לכלום את עצמו, ונתבטל כל עצמותו וגשמיותו, ונתבטל כאלו אינו בעולם, כמו שכתוב (תהלים מ"ד): "כי־עליך הרגנו כל־היום". וזה בחינת (שיר־השירים ה): "שחורות כעורב".
assignments.reason: Total self-nullification — not counting oneself for anything, all physicality annulled, as if one does not exist in the world, 'for Your sake we are killed all day,' 'black as a raven.' This IS the act of self-sacrifice in prayer — the raven quality (פושקנצא) that swallows the serpent of self-interest. Its essential nature is the highest mode of prayer: prayer as mesirut nefesh. The additions file proposes פושקנצא/מסירת נפש for Package 5; this node is the elaborated description of that same quality. It belongs in the prayer/Abraham cluster.

assignments.node_id: חשך, הינו מסירת־נפש, שמשחיר פניו כעורב
assignments.reason: Darkness — that is, self-sacrifice, blackening one's face like a raven. This compound node bridges prayer-as-self-sacrifice and hidden Torah, but its essential name ('חשך') places it in the hidden Torah domain. Package 6 already contains חשך as a node (the darkness that IS the hidden Torah — 'ישת חשך סתרו'). The Rebbe states: 'סתרי תורה אדם זוכה להם על ידי חשך' — hidden Torah is attained THROUGH darkness. Here, the darkness is identified with mesirut nefesh, but the node_id leads with חשך, and its nature is the quality of concealment/depth that characterizes hidden Torah. The self-sacrifice is the means; the darkness is the essential quality of the nistar domain.
